unit.title: B1 Review
unit.subtitle: Capstone: bring all your B1 skills together

grammar.title: Everything you built at B1, in one place
grammar.intro: No new grammar today — this is your capstone. At B1 you learned to express doubt and emotion with the subjunctive, reach further back in time with the pluperfect, report what others said, join ideas with relative and si-clauses, and link it all with connectors. Let's recap the highlights, then mix them together.

sections.heading: Subjunctive: doubt, emotion, wishes
sections.body: After feelings, doubt, and impersonal expressions, the second verb goes into the subjunctive. Also after ojalá and after cuando pointing to the future:

ex.en: I don't think he's coming today.
I'll call you when I arrive.

sections.heading: Pluperfect & reported speech
sections.body: The pluperfect (había + participle) marks the 'past before the past'. In reported speech, tenses shift back a step:

ex.en: When I arrived, the film had already started.
He said he would come late.

sections.heading: Relative & si-clauses + connectors
sections.body: Join sentences with que / lo que. Real conditions use the present; hypothetical ones use si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional. And glue ideas with connectors like sin embargo:

ex.en: That's what I wanted to say.
ex.note: lo que = what / the thing that

ex.en: If I had time, I would travel more.
I wanted to go; however, I was tired.

takeaways: Subjunctive after doubt/emotion/impersonal, ojalá, and future cuando.
Pluperfect = había + participle: the past before the past.
Reported speech shifts tenses back: dijo que vendría.
Relatives: que, lo que. Real si = present; hypothetical si = si tuviera… viajaría.
Connectors (sin embargo, por lo tanto…) link your ideas smoothly.

mistakes.why: 'No creo que' expresses doubt, so it triggers the subjunctive: venga.
A hypothetical 'si' uses the imperfect subjunctive (tuviera), never the conditional.

mistakes.w: Cuando llegué, ya empezó la película.
mistakes.r: Cuando llegué, ya había empezado la película.
mistakes.why: An action finished before another past action needs the pluperfect: había empezado.

exercises.prompt_en: I don't think he's coming today.

exercises.prompt: Cuando llegué, la película ya ___ empezado.
exercises.prompt_en: When I arrived, the film had already started.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! El pasado antes del pasado → pluscuamperfecto: había empezado.
exercises.no: The past before another past uses the pluperfect: “había empezado”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “If I had money, I would travel more.”
exercises.no: Hypothetical: “Si tuviera dinero, viajaría más” — si + tuviera + conditional.

exercises.prompt_en: That's what I wanted to say.
exercises.hint: Two words 'lo ___' mean 'what / the thing that'.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! lo que = what / the thing that.
exercises.no: 'What / the thing that' is “lo que”: eso es lo que quería decir.

exercises.prompt: Match each B1 tool to its use.

exercises.tts: Dijo que vendría cuando terminara el trabajo.
accepted: dijo que vendria cuando terminara el trabajo
exercises.translation: He said he would come when he finished work.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Dijo que vendría cuando terminara el trabajo.”
exercises.no: It was: “Dijo que vendría cuando terminara el trabajo.” (He said he'd come when he finished work.)

exercises.scenario: A friend asks for advice about a job offer 💼

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.es: Me han ofrecido un trabajo en otra ciudad, pero no sé qué hacer.
lines.en: They've offered me a job in another city, but I don't know what to do.

options.text: Te aconsejo que lo pienses bien; si yo estuviera en tu lugar, lo aceptaría.
Te aconsejo que lo piensas bien; si yo estaría en tu lugar, lo aceptaría.
Te aconsejo que lo pensarías bien; si yo estuviera en tu lugar, lo acepto.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Consejo con subjuntivo (que lo pienses) + condición hipotética (si estuviera… aceptaría). ¡Todo el B1 junto!
exercises.no: Advice uses the subjunctive and a hypothetical si-clause: “Te aconsejo que lo pienses bien; si yo estuviera en tu lugar, lo aceptaría.”

exercises.say: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo para viajar.
exercises.en: I wish I had more time to travel.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound.
